title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Procedures for Pretrial Conferences in Criminal Cases and the Procedures for Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the "Procedures for Pre-trial Conferences in Criminal Cases" and the "Procedures for Excluding Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases"

Fa Fa [2024] No. 12

Higher People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), State Security Departments (Bureaus), Judicial Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Military Procuratorate; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; the Public Security Bureau, State Security Bureau, and Judicial Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

To fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, further advance the reform of the trial-centered criminal procedure system, and strictly regulate the procedures for pre-trial conferences and the exclusion of illegal evidence, the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, and Ministry of Justice have, on the basis of the "Procedures for Pre-trial Conferences in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)" and the "Procedures for Excluding Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)," formulated the "Procedures for Pre-trial Conferences in Criminal Cases" and the "Procedures for Excluding Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases." They are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation in light of actual conditions. Any new situations or problems encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported to the central competent authorities through hierarchical channels.

July 25, 2024

Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice

Procedures for Pre-trial Conferences in Criminal Cases

To implement the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, and Ministry of Justice on Advancing the Reform of the Trial-Centered Criminal Procedure System," standardize the procedures for pre-trial conferences, and improve the quality and efficiency of court trials, these Procedures are formulated in accordance with legal provisions and in light of judicial practice.

Article 1. For criminal cases subject to ordinary procedures, if any of the following circumstances exist, the people's court may convene a pre-trial conference before the trial commences:

(1) There are numerous evidentiary materials and the case is of major complexity;

(2) There are significant disputes between the prosecution and defense regarding facts or evidence;

(3) The case has substantial social impact;

(4) Other circumstances requiring the convening of a pre-trial conference.

Article 2. The prosecution or defense may apply to the people's court for the convening of a pre-trial conference. Where an application is made, the matters to be addressed and the reasons therefor shall be stated. If, upon review, the people's court deems it necessary, it shall decide to convene a pre-trial conference; if it decides not to convene one, it shall inform the applicant.

If the defendant or his defense counsel applies for the exclusion of illegal evidence before the trial commences and provides relevant clues or materials in accordance with legal provisions, the people's court shall convene a pre-trial conference.

Article 3. At the pre-trial conference, the people's court may inquire into matters related to the trial, hear opinions, lawfully handle matters that may cause trial interruption, such as jurisdiction, recusal, the list of testifying witnesses, and the exclusion of illegal evidence, organize the prosecution and defense to present evidence, summarize the points of dispute, and carry out mediation for attached civil actions.

Article 4. The pre-trial conference shall be presided over by the presiding judge or the judge handling the case; other judges of the collegial panel may also preside over the pre-trial conference.

The public prosecutor and defense counsel shall participate in the pre-trial conference; prosecutor assistants and legal assistants may assist.

Depending on the circumstances of the case, the defendant may participate in the pre-trial conference; where the defendant applies to participate in the pre-trial conference or applies for the exclusion of illegal evidence, the people's court shall notify the defendant to appear; for cases with multiple defendants, the people's court shall determine the defense counsel and defendants who participate in the pre-trial conference based on the circumstances of the case.

Where a pre-trial conference involves mediation for an attached civil action, the people's court shall notify the parties to the attached civil action and their statutory agents or litigation representatives to appear.

Article 5. If the defendant does not participate in the pre-trial conference, defense counsel shall generally consult the defendant's opinion on matters to be addressed at the pre-trial conference before it is convened.

Article 6. Pre-trial conferences are generally not held in public.

Depending on the circumstances of the case, the people's court may decide to convene the pre-trial conference via video or other means.

Article 7. Depending on the circumstances of the case, pre-trial conferences may be convened multiple times before the trial; after adjournment, a pre-trial conference may be convened before the trial resumes.

Article 8. Pre-trial conferences shall be held in a courtroom or other case-handling venues. If the defendant is in custody and participates, the conference may be held in a courtroom set up within the detention center or other suitable venue.

If a defendant in custody participates in the pre-trial conference, court police shall be present.

Article 9. The people's court shall, based on the circumstances of the case and synthesizing the opinions of the prosecution and defense, determine the main matters to be addressed at the pre-trial conference. Three days before the pre-trial conference is convened, it shall notify the participants of the time, location, participants, and matters of the conference, and inform defense counsel that they may submit a written summary of the key points of defense within three days after the pre-trial conference. Upon receipt of the written summary, the people's court shall promptly send a copy to the people's procuratorate. Such notifications shall be recorded in the case file.

Article 10. After the pre-trial conference begins, the presiding person shall verify the participants' presence and announce the matters to be addressed at the pre-trial conference.

If multiple defendants participate in the pre-trial conference, measures shall be taken to prevent collusion.

Article 11. At the pre-trial conference, the presiding person may inquire about the following matters and hear opinions from the prosecution and defense:

(1) Whether there is any objection to the jurisdiction of the case;

(2) Whether an application for recusal of relevant personnel is made;

(3) Whether an application for a closed trial is made;

(4) Whether an application for the exclusion of illegal evidence is made;

(5) Whether new evidentiary materials are provided;

(6) Whether an application for retrial or re-inspection is made;

(7) Whether an application is made for the obtainment of evidentiary materials collected by the public security or procuratorial organs during investigation or examination of prosecution but not transferred with the case, that prove the defendant's innocence or lesser guilt;

(8) Whether an application is made to collect or obtain evidentiary materials from witnesses or relevant units or individuals;

(9) Whether an application is made for witnesses, expert witnesses, persons with specialized knowledge, investigators, or other persons to appear in court, and whether there is any objection to the list of appearing persons;

(10) Whether there is any objection to the ownership of property involved in the case and to the handling recommendations of the people's procuratorate;

(11) Other issues related to the trial.

At the pre-trial conference, the people's court may carry out mediation for attached civil actions.

For matters listed in paragraph 1 that may cause trial interruption, the prosecution and defense shall clearly state whether they intend to raise relevant applications or requests. The people's court may lawfully make a ruling and explain the ruling and reasons at trial.

Article 12. If the defendant or his defense counsel raises an objection to the jurisdiction of the case, reasons shall be provided. Upon review, if the people's court finds the objection justified, it shall lawfully return the case to the people's procuratorate or transfer it to a higher people's court with jurisdiction; if it finds itself not suitable to exercise jurisdiction, it may request the higher people's court to handle the matter. If the people's court finds the objection unfounded, it shall lawfully reject the objection.

Article 13. If the defendant or his defense counsel applies for recusal of members of the collegial panel, judge assistants, court clerks, expert witnesses, or interpreters, reasons shall be provided. Upon review, if the people's court finds the application justified, it shall lawfully decide on the recusal of the relevant person; if it finds the application unfounded, it shall lawfully reject the application.

If the defendant or his defense counsel applies for the recusal of a procurator, and the circumstances are those prescribed in Articles 29 and 30 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the people's procuratorate shall lawfully decide on the recusal or rejection of the application.

If the application for recusal by the defendant or his defense counsel is rejected, they may apply for one reconsideration upon receiving the decision. For circumstances not falling under Articles 29 and 30 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the people's court shall reject the application, and the defendant or his defense counsel may not apply for reconsideration.

Article 14. If the prosecution or defense applies for a closed trial, the people's court shall approve if, upon review, it finds that the case involves state secrets or personal privacy; it may approve if it finds that the case involves trade secrets.

Article 15. If the defendant or his defense counsel applies for the exclusion of illegal evidence before the trial and provides relevant clues or materials in accordance with legal provisions, the people's court shall, three days before the pre-trial conference is convened, send copies of the application and relevant clues or materials to the people's procuratorate. At the pre-trial conference, the people's procuratorate shall, by presenting relevant evidentiary materials and other means, specifically explain the legality of the evidence collection. The people's court may verify the relevant evidentiary materials; upon application by the prosecution or defense, it may selectively play audiovisual recordings of interrogations. When necessary, it may notify investigators or other persons to participate in the pre-trial conference to provide explanations.

The people's procuratorate may withdraw the relevant evidence. Withdrawn evidence may not be presented at trial without new reasons. The defendant or his defense counsel may withdraw the application for exclusion of illegal evidence. After withdrawal, without new clues or materials, no further application for exclusion of the relevant evidence may be made.

If the prosecution and defense fail to reach consensus at the pre-trial conference on the legality of evidence collection, and the people's court has doubts about the legality of the evidence collection, it shall conduct an investigation at trial; if there are no doubts about the legality of the evidence collection and there are no new clues or materials indicating possible illegal evidence collection, it may decide not to conduct an investigation and state the reasons.

Article 16. If the prosecution or defense applies for retrial or re-inspection, reasons shall be provided. Upon review, if the people's court deems it necessary, it shall approve the application.

Article 17. If the defendant or his defense counsel makes a written application for the obtainment of evidentiary materials that were collected by the public security or procuratorial organs during investigation or examination of prosecution but not transferred with the case, and that prove the defendant's innocence or lesser guilt, and provides relevant clues or materials, the people's court shall obtain them and notify the people's procuratorate to transfer them within three days of receiving the written decision. If not transferred, the people's procuratorate shall provide a written explanation of the relevant circumstances.

If the defendant or his defense counsel applies to collect or obtain evidentiary materials from witnesses or relevant units or individuals, reasons shall be provided. Upon review, if the people's court finds that the relevant evidentiary materials may affect the determination of guilt or sentencing, it shall approve; if it finds that the evidentiary materials are irrelevant to the case or manifestly redundant or unnecessary, it may not approve.

Article 18. If the prosecution or defense applies for witnesses, expert witnesses, persons with specialized knowledge, or investigators to appear in court, reasons shall be provided. Upon review, if the people's court finds the reasons justified, it shall notify the relevant persons to appear.

If the prosecution or defense has objections to the list of appearing witnesses, expert witnesses, persons with specialized knowledge, or investigators, the people's court shall, upon review, if it finds the objections justified, lawfully make a ruling; if it finds the objections unfounded, it shall lawfully reject them.

After the people's court notifies witnesses, expert witnesses, persons with specialized knowledge, or investigators to appear, the prosecution and defense shall assist in ensuring their appearance.

Article 19. Before the pre-trial conference is convened, the people's procuratorate shall transfer all evidentiary materials to the people's court, and the defendant or his defense counsel shall submit all evidentiary materials that prove the defendant's innocence or absence of criminal responsibility, such as evidence that the defendant was not at the crime scene, had not reached the age of criminal responsibility, or was a legally irresponsible mental patient.

After receiving the evidentiary materials transferred or submitted by the prosecution or defense, the people's court shall notify the other party to review, extract, and copy them.

Article 20. At the pre-trial conference, for evidence that the prosecution and defense decide to present at trial, the people's court may organize the presentation of such evidence, with the presenting party briefly explaining the content the evidence proves and hearing the other party's opinions, and sort out the evidence in dispute. The prosecution and defense shall not cross-examine or debate.

For evidence on which the prosecution and defense have no dispute at the pre-trial conference, the presentation and cross-examination at trial may be simplified.

Article 21. The people's court may, at the pre-trial conference, hear the opinions of the prosecution and defense and summarize the points of dispute. Matters on which there is no dispute or consensus between the prosecution and defense may be simplified at trial.

The people's court may organize the prosecution and defense to negotiate and determine matters such as the order and method of presenting evidence at trial, and clarify the method and focus of the in-court investigation. Matters on which consensus cannot be reached shall be determined by the people's court.

Article 22. For cases where the defendant did not plead guilty before the pre-trial conference but pleads guilty during the pre-trial conference, after the people's court verifies the voluntariness and truthfulness of the guilty plea and hears opinions from the prosecution and defense, the trial may be simplified.

Article 23. After hearing the opinions of the prosecution and defense on the facts and evidence of the case at the pre-trial conference, if the case is clearly insufficient in facts or evidence, the people's court may suggest that the people's procuratorate supplement materials or withdraw the prosecution. For cases where withdrawal is suggested and the people's procuratorate does not agree, after the trial begins, without new facts or reasons, withdrawal of prosecution is generally not permitted.

Article 24. Minutes of the pre-trial conference shall be made and signed by the participants after verification.

After the pre-trial conference concludes, the people's court shall prepare a pre-trial conference report, setting forth the basic circumstances of the pre-trial conference, the results of handling matters related to the trial, the points of dispute between the prosecution and defense, and any consensus reached on relevant matters.

Article 25. For cases where a pre-trial conference is held, after the indictment is read, the court shall announce the main contents of the pre-trial conference report.

For matters such as handling objections to jurisdiction, applications for recusal, or applications for a closed trial, the court may announce the relevant contents of the pre-trial conference report after informing the parties of their procedural rights.

For cases involving multiple criminal facts, when necessary, the relevant contents of the pre-trial conference report may be announced again before the start of the in-court investigation of the relevant criminal facts.

Article 26. After announcing the pre-trial conference report, for matters on which the prosecution and defense have reached consensus or on which the people's court has made a ruling, the court shall, after briefly verifying with the prosecution and defense, confirm them at trial. Unless there are valid reasons, such matters shall generally not be handled again; for other matters, the court shall handle them lawfully.

Article 27. The people's court of second instance shall refer to the above provisions when convening a pre-trial conference.

Article 28. These Procedures shall take effect from September 3, 2024. The "Procedures for Pre-trial Conferences in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)" shall be simultaneously abolished.

Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice

Procedures for Excluding Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases

To implement the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, and Ministry of Justice on Advancing the Reform of the Trial-Centered Criminal Procedure System" and the "Provisions on Strictly Excluding Illegal Evidence in the Handling of Criminal Cases," standardize the procedures for excluding illegal evidence, accurately punish crimes, and effectively safeguard human rights, these Procedures are formulated in accordance with legal provisions and in light of judicial practice.

Article 1. Confessions of a criminal suspect or defendant collected by any of the following illegal methods shall be excluded:

(1) Confessions made against the will of the criminal suspect or defendant, causing unbearable pain, by means of violence such as beating or illegal use of restraint devices, or by harsh means constituting disguised corporal punishment;

(2) Confessions made against the will of the criminal suspect or defendant, causing unbearable pain, by means of threats such as violence or serious damage to the lawful rights and interests of the person or his close relatives;

(3) Confessions of a criminal suspect or defendant collected by illegal restriction of personal liberty, such as illegal detention.

Where a confession is made by a criminal suspect or defendant under torture, subsequent repeated confessions influenced by the torture shall also be excluded, except in the following circumstances:

(1) During the investigation period, after the investigative organ confirms or cannot exclude that evidence was collected by illegal means based on complaints, reports, or its own discovery, and replaces the investigator, and other investigators, during a subsequent interrogation, inform the criminal suspect or defendant of his procedural rights and the legal consequences of a guilty plea, and the criminal suspect or defendant voluntarily confesses;

(2) During the period for review of arrest, examination of prosecution, or trial, if the procurator or judge, during interrogation, informs the criminal suspect or defendant of his procedural rights and the legal consequences of a guilty plea, and the criminal suspect or defendant voluntarily confesses.

Article 2. Witness testimony or victim statements collected by illegal methods such as violence, threats, or illegal restriction of personal liberty shall be excluded.

Article 3. Physical evidence or documentary evidence collected by illegal search, seizure, or other methods violating legal procedures, which may seriously affect judicial justice, shall be rectified or reasonably explained; if unable to be rectified or reasonably explained, such evidence shall be excluded.

Article 4. For cases that may be punishable by life imprisonment or the death penalty, or other major cases, before the conclusion of the investigation, the investigative organ shall notify in writing the procurator stationed at the detention center of the people's procuratorate to conduct a review of the legality of the interrogation. The procurator shall, before the conclusion of the investigation, question the criminal suspect to verify whether there were illegal evidence-gathering methods such as torture, and shall make an audiovisual recording of the entire process.

Article 5. After the review is completed, the people's procuratorate shall prepare a written review opinion on the legality of the interrogation in major cases and serve it on the investigative organ. Where the review confirms or cannot exclude illegal evidence-gathering methods such as torture, the investigative organ shall be notified to lawfully exclude illegal evidence. If the investigative organ has no objection to the existence of torture or other illegal evidence-gathering, or after re-examination confirms such illegal evidence-gathering, it shall promptly exclude the illegal evidence lawfully and shall not use it as a basis for requesting approval of arrest or transferring for prosecution, and shall prepare a notice of the results of the illegal evidence exclusion, informing the people's procuratorate of the exclusion of illegal evidence. The review opinion on the legality of the interrogation in major cases and the excluded illegal evidence shall be transferred with the case, with a notation that they are lawfully excluded illegal evidence.

Article 6. When handling cases for review of arrest or examination of prosecution, if the people's procuratorate discovers that investigators have collected evidence by illegal methods, it shall promptly investigate and verify; if the criminal suspect or his defense counsel applies for exclusion of illegal evidence and provides clues or materials such as the identity of the person allegedly involved in illegal evidence collection, as well as the time, place, method, and content, the people's procuratorate shall accept and review the application. If, based on existing materials, the legality of the evidence collection cannot be proven, the people's procuratorate shall promptly conduct an investigation and verification.

If the people's procuratorate believes that there may be illegal evidence collection methods such as torture, it may request in writing that the investigative organ provide an explanation of the legality of the evidence collection. Where illegal evidence collection methods are indeed found, the people's procuratorate shall lawfully issue a corrective opinion to the investigative organ.

Article 7. During the period of examination of prosecution, if the people's procuratorate, upon review, finds that there is indeed torture or other illegal evidence collection, or cannot exclude such a possibility, it shall lawfully exclude the illegal evidence and shall not use it as a basis for initiating a public prosecution. The people's procuratorate may require the investigative organ to reassign investigators to recollect evidence, and may also conduct its own investigation and evidence collection when necessary.

The people's procuratorate shall transfer the excluded illegal evidence with the case, stating that it is lawfully excluded illegal evidence, and shall also transfer the audiovisual recordings of interrogations and relevant case files to the people's court.

Article 8 A criminal suspect, defendant, or defense counsel applying for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence shall provide relevant clues or materials. "Clues" refers to specific content with clear targets, such as the personnel, time, place, and method suspected of illegal evidence collection. "Materials" refers to evidence that reflects illegal evidence collection, such as photographs of injuries, physical examination records, hospital medical records, interrogation transcripts, interrogation audio-video recordings, or testimony of cellmates.

Article 9 When serving the indictment copy to the defendant and defense counsel, the People's Court shall inform them of the right to apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the trial begins and to simultaneously provide relevant clues or materials. The above circumstances shall be recorded in the case file.

Article 10 The defendant and defense counsel shall apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the trial begins, except where relevant clues or materials are discovered during the trial.

The defendant and defense counsel applying for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence shall submit a written application to the People's Court. If the defendant has difficulty in writing, an oral application may be made, but it shall be recorded in the case file and signed or fingerprinted by the defendant.

If the defendant applies for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence but has no defense counsel, the People's Court shall notify the legal aid institution to assign a lawyer to provide defense.

Article 11 If the defendant and defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provide relevant clues or materials, the People's Court shall hold a pre-trial conference and, three days before the conference, send copies of the application and relevant clues or materials to the People's Procuratorate.

If the defendant and defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence but fail to provide relevant clues or materials, the People's Court shall inform them to supplement submission. If they do not supplement, the People's Court shall not accept the application and shall notify the defendant and defense counsel before the trial begins. The above circumstances shall be recorded in the case file.

If the defendant, when questioned by the People's Procuratorate to verify the legality of interrogation, clearly states that there was no illegal evidence collection such as torture during the investigation stage, but later raises an application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence at the trial stage, reasons shall be provided. If the People's Court, upon review, has no doubt about the legality of evidence collection, it may reject the application.

Article 12 If the defendant applies for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, the People's Court shall notify the defendant to attend the pre-trial conference.

Article 13 Before the pre-trial conference, the presiding judge handling the case shall review the case files and examine the legality of evidence collection:

(1) Whether the defendant raised an application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence during the investigation or review and prosecution stage; if so, whether relevant clues or materials were provided;

(2) Whether the investigation authority or People's Procuratorate conducted an investigation and verification of the legality of evidence collection; if so, whether an investigation conclusion was made;

(3) For major cases, whether the People's Procuratorate's stationed detention center inspector verified the legality of interrogation before the conclusion of the investigation, and whether the verification process was simultaneously audio-video recorded; if verification was conducted, whether a verification opinion on the legality of interrogation in major cases was produced;

(4) Whether evidence excluded by the People's Procuratorate as illegal during the review of arrest and review of prosecution stages is transferred with the case file and clearly indicated as illegally obtained evidence that has been excluded.

If after reviewing the legality of evidence collection, the People's Court deems it necessary to supplement the above evidentiary materials, it shall notify the People's Procuratorate to provide them within three days.

Article 14 During the pre-trial conference, when the People's Court examines the legality of evidence collection, it generally follows these steps:

(1) The defendant and defense counsel read out the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provide relevant clues or materials;

(2) The prosecutor presents evidentiary materials proving the legality of evidence collection;

(3) The prosecution and defense present their opinions on the legality of evidence collection;

(4) If the prosecution and defense fail to reach an agreement on the legality of evidence collection, the presiding judge summarizes the points of dispute.

Article 15 During the pre-trial conference, the People's Procuratorate shall, by presenting relevant evidentiary materials and other means, provide a targeted explanation of the legality of evidence collection. The People's Court may verify the relevant materials, and at the request of either the prosecution or defense, may play targeted interrogation audio-video recordings. When necessary, it may notify investigators or other personnel to attend the pre-trial conference to explain the situation.

Article 16 During the pre-trial conference, the People's Procuratorate may withdraw relevant evidence. Withdrawn evidence shall not be presented at trial without new reasons.

The defendant and defense counsel may withdraw the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence. After withdrawal, without new clues or materials, no further application for exclusion of the relevant evidence shall be made.

Article 17 If the prosecution and defense reach an agreement on the legality of evidence collection during the pre-trial conference, but one party later reneges at trial, the court generally shall not conduct a further review, except for legitimate reasons.

If the prosecution and defense fail to reach an agreement on the legality of evidence collection during the pre-trial conference, and the People's Court has doubts about the legality of evidence collection, it shall conduct an investigation during the trial; if it has no doubt about the legality of evidence collection and there are no new clues or materials indicating possible illegal evidence collection, it may decide not to conduct an investigation and shall explain the reasons.

Article 18 The presiding judge shall include in the pre-trial conference report a description of the review of the legality of evidence collection, mainly including the points of dispute between the prosecution and defense and the agreements reached on relevant matters.

Article 19 If the defendant and defense counsel do not apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the trial begins but raise the application during the trial, reasons shall be provided. If the People's Court, upon review, has doubts about the legality of evidence collection, it shall conduct an investigation; if it has no doubt, it shall reject the application.

After the People's Court rejects the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, if the defendant and defense counsel reapply on the same grounds without new clues or materials, the People's Court shall not review the application again.

Article 20 If the People's Court decides to conduct a court investigation into the legality of evidence collection, it shall first conduct an investigation during the trial. For circumstances such as where the evidence sought to be excluded is unrelated to other criminal facts, to prevent excessive delay of the trial, the court may first investigate other criminal facts and then investigate the legality of evidence collection.

Before the court investigation procedure on the legality of evidence collection concludes, the relevant evidence shall not be presented or examined.

Article 21 When the court decides to investigate the legality of evidence collection, it generally follows these steps:

(1) For cases where a pre-trial conference has been held, after reading the indictment, the court shall announce the review of the legality of evidence collection at the pre-trial conference and the points of dispute between the prosecution and defense;

(2) The defendant and defense counsel explain the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and the relevant clues or materials;

(3) The prosecutor presents evidentiary materials proving the legality of evidence collection; the defendant and defense counsel may cross-examine the relevant evidence. With the permission of the presiding judge, the prosecutor and defense counsel may question the investigators or other personnel present in court;

(4) The prosecution and defense debate the legality of evidence collection.

Article 22 The burden of proof for the legality of evidence collection shall be borne by the People's Procuratorate.

To prove the legality of evidence collection, the prosecutor may present evidentiary materials such as interrogation transcripts, detention records, physical examination records, legal documents on compulsory measures or investigative measures, verification materials on the legality of interrogation, and may also play interrogation audio-video recordings for the interrogation periods challenged by the defendant and defense counsel, and request the court to notify relevant investigators or other personnel to appear in court to explain the situation.

During the trial, if the prosecutor discovers that evidence cannot be presented at the current hearing or that supplementary investigation is needed to provide new evidence, and requests an adjournment, the court may adjourn the trial.

Article 23 The defendant and defense counsel may present relevant clues or materials and request the court to play interrogation audio-video recordings for specific interrogation periods.

If the defendant and defense counsel request the People's Court to obtain interrogation audio-video recordings, physical examination records, and other evidentiary materials collected but not submitted by the investigation authority or People's Procuratorate, the People's Court shall, upon review, obtain them if it determines that the materials are related to the legality of evidence collection; if it determines that the materials are unrelated to the legality of evidence collection, it shall decide not to obtain them and explain the reasons to the defendant and defense counsel.

If the defendant and defense counsel request the People's Court to notify investigators or other personnel to appear in court to explain the situation, and the People's Court deems it truly necessary, it shall notify the aforesaid personnel to appear in court, and shall not substitute an explanation signed and sealed by the investigators.

Article 24 When investigating the legality of evidence collection, the court shall focus on examining interrogation audio-video recordings, prioritizing the review of the following content:

(1) Whether the interrogation audio-video recording was produced in accordance with the law. For cases where a sentence of life imprisonment or death may be imposed, or other major criminal cases, whether the interrogation process was audio-video recorded;

(2) Whether the interrogation audio-video recording is complete. Whether each interrogation session was audio-video recorded, whether the recording was continuous without interruption, and whether there were circumstances such as selective recording, editing, or deletion;

(3) Whether the interrogation audio-video recording was made simultaneously. Whether the recording began at the start of the interrogation and ended after the criminal suspect reviewed and signed the interrogation transcript; whether the start and end times recorded in the interrogation transcript are consistent with those reflected in the audio-video recording;

(4) Whether there are differences between the interrogation audio-video recording and the interrogation transcript. For content related to conviction and sentencing, whether there are substantive differences between the interrogation transcript and the audio-video recording; if substantive differences exist, the audio-video recording shall prevail.

Article 25 If investigators or other personnel appear in court, they shall explain the evidence collection process to the court and accept questions from the prosecution and defense on relevant circumstances. If the manner of questioning is inappropriate or the content is unrelated to the legality of evidence collection, the court shall stop it.

If, after being notified by the People's Court, an investigator fails to appear in court to explain the situation, and the possibility of obtaining evidence by illegal methods cannot be excluded, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

Article 26 If the People's Court has doubts about the source or content of evidence provided by the prosecution and defense, it may inform them to supplement evidence or provide explanations; when necessary, it may adjourn the hearing to investigate and verify the evidence. When investigating and verifying evidence outside the court, the court may notify the prosecution and defense to be present and shall record the verification process in the case file.

Evidence supplemented by the prosecution and defense or obtained through the court's out-of-court investigation and verification, unless it has been verified through court procedures such as presentation and cross-examination, shall not be used as a basis for proving the legality of evidence collection. However, exceptions apply if the prosecution and defense have no objection after out-of-court consultation.

Article 27 After trial, if the defendant's confession falls under any of the following circumstances, it shall be excluded:

(1) It is confirmed that the evidence was collected by illegal methods as specified in Article 1 of these Rules;

(2) For cases where interrogation should have been audio-video recorded, no interrogation audio-video recording was provided, or the recording had selective recording, editing, deletion, or other issues, and based on the overall available evidence, the possibility of collecting evidence by illegal methods cannot be excluded;

(3) The investigation authority conducted interrogations outside the designated case processing premises except in emergency situations, and based on the overall available evidence, the possibility of collecting evidence by illegal methods cannot be excluded;

(4) Other circumstances where the possibility of collecting evidence by illegal methods cannot be excluded.

Article 28 After investigating the legality of evidence collection, the People's Court shall make a decision in court on whether to exclude the relevant evidence. When necessary, it may adjourn the hearing for the collegiate bench to deliberate or submit to the adjudicative committee for discussion, announcing the decision when the hearing resumes.

Illegally obtained evidence that has been excluded in accordance with the law shall not be presented or cross-examined and shall not be used as a basis for adjudication.

Article 29 The People's Court's conclusions on the review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection shall be stated in the judgment document, along with the reasons.

Article 30 If the People's Procuratorate, the defendant, or his legal representative files a protest or appeal, challenging the first-instance People's Court's conclusions on the review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection, the second-instance People's Court shall review the issue.

Article 31 The People's Procuratorate shall comprehensively present evidentiary materials proving the legality of evidence collection during the first-instance proceedings.

If the People's Procuratorate failed to present such evidentiary materials during the first-instance proceedings, and the first-instance People's Court lawfully excluded the relevant evidence, the People's Procuratorate shall not present the previously unsubmitted evidentiary materials during the second-instance proceedings, except for materials discovered after the first-instance proceedings.

Article 32 If the defendant and defense counsel did not apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence during the first-instance proceedings but raise the application during the second-instance proceedings, the second-instance People's Court shall review the application under any of the following circumstances:

(1) The first-instance People's Court failed to inform the defendant of the right to apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence in accordance with the law;

(2) The defendant and defense counsel discovered relevant clues or materials suggesting illegal evidence collection after the first-instance trial.

Article 33 If the first-instance People's Court fails to review the defendant and defense counsel's application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and uses the relevant evidence as a basis for adjudication, potentially affecting a fair trial, the second-instance People's Court shall rule to quash the original judgment and remand the case to the original People's Court for retrial.

Article 34 If the first-instance People's Court fails to exclude illegally obtained evidence that should have been excluded in accordance with the law, the second-instance People's Court may lawfully exclude the illegally obtained evidence. After excluding the illegally obtained evidence, the case shall be handled according to law depending on the specific circumstances.

Article 35 The People's Court's review and investigation procedures for the legality of evidence collection regarding witness testimony, victim statements, and other evidence shall apply the above provisions by reference.

Review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection during second-instance proceedings, trial supervision proceedings, and death penalty review proceedings shall apply the above provisions by reference.

Article 36 These Rules shall take effect on September 3, 2024. The Procedures for the People's Courts in Handling Criminal Cases to Exclude Illegally Obtained Evidence (Trial) shall be simultaneously abolished.
